title: Weekend Plans
description: Discuss abilities, preferences, current actions, and a simple weekend plan.
objectives: Discuss abilities, preferences, current actions, and a simple weekend plan.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to discuss abilities, preferences, current actions, and a simple weekend plan. The central language is integrated free-time review. It belongs to the practical context of free time & abilities. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.english: Can you play tennis on Saturday?
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the weekend plans exchange.

blocks.english: Yes, let's meet at the park.
blocks.explanation: This weekend plans model adds a different detail or response.

blocks.english: What do you like to do?
blocks.explanation: Use this question or response to keep the weekend plans exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “Can you play tennis on Saturday?” and “Yes, let's meet at the park.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: integrated free-time review.
